headline: Measured against the same point in 2024, every comparable measure is more Democratic. Measured against 2022, it isn't, because Democrats have moved from mail ballots to voting early in person.

compare_note: Democratic share of mail-ballot requests (CNN/Catalist, Oct 1). Gray dot is the same point in 2024. Virginia's early voters with only Democratic primary history lead those with only GOP history by 18 points, vs. 8 in 2024; Ohio's early electorate is about 27 points more Democratic than at this point in 2024 (CNN, Oct 8). CNN also found that the 2022 request pools were more Democratic than 2026's in every listed state except Iowa.

bullets.title: The edge over 2024 is real but partly a change in how Democrats vote.
bullets.html: Democratic mail requests in North Carolina are down 40% from 2022, against 18% for Republicans, yet Democrats are returning ballots faster (22% returned vs. 17% in 2022). In an NBC poll, 23% of Democrats plan to vote by mail, down from 34% in 2024, and 36% plan to vote early in person, up from 30%. Democrats' confidence that the Postal Service will deliver ballots on time fell from 86% to 60% (Marist).

bullets.title: Volume against 2022 is mixed.
bullets.html: Michigan's returned absentee ballots are up 30% from the same point in 2022 (201,909 vs. 155,142) and Minnesota's up 29% (127,682 vs. 99,252). North Carolina is 22.5% behind (27,854 vs. 35,958).

bullets.title: Virginia is more Democratic but slower.
bullets.html: State Navigate estimates its early vote is 4.2 points more Democratic than 2025's (6.5 in VA-1, 8.6 in VA-9). Turnout runs 23% behind the same point in 2024, per TargetSmart.

bullets.title: The early electorate is old.
bullets.html: Voters 65 and older cast about two-thirds of returned ballots in Michigan, Pennsylvania and Georgia; 18–25s cast 2–6%. It will get younger as in-person voting opens.

bullets.title: Democratic data firms report a Latino and Black surge.
bullets.html: TargetSmart's Tom Bonier says the Hispanic share of the early vote is above the same point in 2022 in more than 94% of 229 comparable counties, with about 112,000 Latino early votes vs. 106,000 at this point in 2024. No independent replication yet.

bullets.title: Republicans say they vote later.
bullets.html: National Review's Noah Rothman argues Democrats will lead the early vote, "but perhaps not by the margins the party expects," because their own warnings eroded trust in mail. A Virginia GOP volunteer told the Daily Signal that "Republicans show up on Election Day more so." No quantitative RNC early-vote claims for 2026 turned up.

bullets.title: Nevada is the cautionary tale.
bullets.html: Its first 2,851 ballots were 48% Democratic and 22% Republican; Jon Ralston called that meaningless this early. In 2024 Democrats led Nevada's mail vote, Republicans led the total early vote, and Trump won.

calendar_note: Iowa and Kansas mail ballots go out Oct 14. Pennsylvania and New Hampshire have no early in-person voting.
cast_at_note: Ballots counted (UF Election Lab, 34 states + DC, state data as of Oct 5-12) when these comparisons were compiled; sets the automatic early-vote weight.
